title: Location Data Disclosure
description: The external entity (Child's device) shares live GPS coordinates with the backend at regular intervals. This act of sharing causes a threat because the data is transmitted in transit, potentially allowing the backend to link or identify the user via the device's identity or metadata.
assumptions: The device is authenticated and the backend has access to the device's unique identifier.

title: Data Linking via Metadata
description: The data flow transmits live GPS coordinates. The threat arises at the data flow level because the transmission of this data (meta-data) allows the backend to link or identify the user based on the device's identity or other metadata associated with the GPS data.
assumptions: The backend has access to device metadata during transmission.

title: Data Disclosure
description: Process P1 writes location pings to DataStore DS1. This constitutes a data disclosure as the process transfers personal data (location pings) to a third-party data store, which may be considered a known or unknown third party depending on the store's nature. The minimality principle is key: only strictly required personal data should be disclosed.
assumptions: The location pings contain personal data.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the data store is considered a 'known third party' under the specific LINDDUN Pro definition of data disclosure, as the store's identity and data retention policies are not fully specified in the context.

title: Linking Threat
description: Data in transit (DF2) carries metadata about the parties involved (Process P1 and DataStore DS1). This metadata could be used to link or identify the data subjects, creating a privacy risk during transmission.
assumptions: The data flow carries metadata that could be used for identification.
uncertainty_note: Assumes standard data-centric threats apply to the transmission of process and data identifiers.

title: Data Disclosure
description: DataStore DS1 receives the location pings and stores them. Storing personal data in a data store without explicit consent or a defined purpose for retention may constitute a data disclosure threat, as the store's processing of this data could be considered a third-party action.
assumptions: The store's storage of the data is considered a processing action by a third party.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the store's storage is considered a 'third party' action under the specific LINDDUN Pro definition of data disclosure, as the store's identity and data retention policies are not fully specified in the context.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The mobile app (P1) shares personal location data with the backend (P1) for processing, which constitutes a data disclosure as the data is transferred to a known third party (the backend) for processing.

title: Linking
description: The data flow (DF3) transmits location pings to the backend, potentially allowing the backend to link or identify the user via meta-data about the parties being used to link them.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The geofencing engine (P2) receives the location pings and processes them to check zone entry/exit, which involves processing personal data in a way that causes a threat.

title: Unauthorized Access to Geofencing Data
description: The Family Account Store (DS2) shares configured zone definitions (home, school, friend's house) with the Geofencing & Alert Engine (P2). If DS2 is not properly secured or if the zone definitions are not encrypted, an unauthorized party could access this data and potentially use it to identify or track individuals.
assumptions: DS2 is accessible to external entities without proper authentication.

title: Data in Transit Identification
description: The zone definitions (home, school, friend's house) are transmitted from DS2 to P2 via the data flow (DF4). If the zone definitions contain identifying metadata (e.g., IP addresses, device IDs, or specific user identifiers) that are not obfuscated, the data in transit could be used to link or identify the parties involved in the data flow.
assumptions: Zone definitions contain identifying metadata.

title: Unauthorized Processing of Geofencing Data
description: The Geofencing & Alert Engine (P2) receives the zone definitions from DS2. If P2 processes or stores this data in a way that causes a threat (e.g., storing it in a database that is accessible to unauthorized users, or using it for purposes not intended by the owner), a privacy threat arises at the destination.
assumptions: P2 processes the data in a way that causes a threat.

title: Unauthorized Access to Geofencing Data
description: The Process (P2) shares arrival/departure notification data with the ExternalEntity (EE1) without verifying the recipient's identity or authorization. This allows EE1 to potentially access sensitive location data for unauthorized purposes.
assumptions: No authentication or authorization mechanism is in place between P2 and EE1.

title: Data in Transit: Unencrypted Transmission
description: The data flow (DF5) transmits arrival/departure notification data in an unencrypted format. This exposes the content of the notifications to interception by third parties.
assumptions: No encryption or secure transmission protocol is configured for this flow.

title: Unauthorized Processing of Location Data
description: The ExternalEntity (EE1) receives the notification data and processes it without any validation of the data's origin or purpose. This allows EE1 to store or use the location data for its own purposes without consent.
assumptions: EE1 has no policy or technical controls to verify the data's legitimacy.

title: Identity Disclosure
description: Parent (EE1) shares its identity (name, DOB, school) with the Mobile App Backend (P1) to create the child's profile. This is a valid interaction (Process->Process) and the threat arises at the source element where the act of sharing causes the exposure of sensitive personal data.

title: Data Processing/Storage
description: The Mobile App Backend (P1) receives the parent's identity data and stores it in a way that causes a threat. This is a valid interaction (Process->Process) and the threat arises at the destination element where the recipient processes or stores the data.

title: Data Disclosure
description: Process P1 (Mobile App Backend) shares account, child profile, and geofence zone data with DataStore DS2. This constitutes a data disclosure as the process transfers personal data across a boundary to a data store.
assumptions: The data is considered personal data (account, child profile, geofence zone) and is required for the service.

title: Data Disclosure in Transit
description: Data-centric threat: The data flow DF7 carries personal data (account, child profile, geofence zone) in transit. The metadata associated with this flow (e.g., data types, parties involved) could be used to identify or link the data recipients, constituting a data disclosure risk.
assumptions: The data in transit is identifiable by its content or associated metadata.

title: Data Disclosure
description: DataStore DS2 receives the data from Process P1. The store's processing or storage of this data could lead to further disclosure or unauthorized access, constituting a data disclosure risk.
assumptions: The store's storage practices or access controls are not fully secure.

title: Location Data Disclosure
description: Parent (EE1) shares its current location or location history with the Mobile App Backend (P1) without explicit consent or a data-sharing agreement. This act of sharing causes a privacy threat as the parent entity is disclosing sensitive personal information.

title: Location Data Transmission
description: The data flow (DF8) transmits location data (current location or history) from the Parent (EE1) to the Mobile App Backend (P1). The transmission itself carries the data-centric threat of potential metadata leakage or the risk of the data being intercepted or misused during transit.

title: Unauthorized Location Processing
description: The Mobile App Backend (P1) receives the location data and processes or stores it in a way that causes a privacy threat. This could include storing location history for future use, sharing it with third parties, or using it for non-consensual tracking.

title: Unauthorized Access to Location History
description: The data store (DS1) shares location history data with the mobile app backend (P1) without explicit user consent or authentication verification. This allows the backend to access sensitive personal location data that the parent user may not intend to share.
assumptions: The system assumes the parent user has granted broad permissions to the backend service.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the backend service has a separate authentication mechanism to verify the parent's identity and consent before accessing the data.

title: Data Linking via Metadata
description: The data flow (DF9) transmits location history data to the backend. The metadata associated with this flow (e.g., source IP, user agent, or device fingerprint) could be used to link or identify the parent user with the mobile app backend, potentially enabling cross-device tracking.
assumptions: The backend service correlates data flows based on metadata, which may not be strictly necessary for this specific interaction.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the backend service relies on metadata for correlation in this specific context.

title: Unauthorized Data Processing
description: The mobile app backend (P1) receives the location history data and processes it to serve the parent's map/history view. This processing may involve storing, aggregating, or analyzing the data in ways that compromise user privacy, such as creating a persistent profile of the user's location history.
assumptions: The backend service processes the data without additional user consent or explicit purpose limitation.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the backend service has a clear, documented purpose for processing this specific data.

title: Identity Disclosure
description: The parent entity (EE1) shares its identity (e.g., name, contact info, or other identifying attributes) with the mobile app backend (P1) to facilitate the invitation process. This action causes a privacy threat because the recipient (P1) may use this information to link or identify the parent, potentially violating the parent's privacy rights.
assumptions: The parent entity has a modeled identity that can be exposed during the interaction.

title: Data Linking
description: The data flow (DF10) transmits meta-data about the parties involved (e.g., the parent's identity and the mobile app's identity) in transit. This data-centric threat arises because the mobile app backend (P1) may use this meta-data to link the parent to the app, potentially enabling tracking or identification of the parent.
assumptions: The mobile app backend processes or stores meta-data about the parties being used to link or identify them.

title: Unauthorized Processing
description: The destination element (P1) receives the parent's identity and processes or stores it in a way that causes a privacy threat. The mobile app backend may use this data to link the parent to the app, potentially violating the parent's privacy rights.
assumptions: The mobile app backend processes or stores the parent's identity in a way that causes a privacy threat.

title: Unauthorized Access
description: The backend process (P1) grants access to the secondary guardian (EE3), which is an external entity. This interaction is invalid per the mapping table (Process->ExternalEntity is not a valid interaction type), meaning the backend does not have a modeled flow to share data with an external entity. The act of sharing data with an external entity without a valid modeled flow creates a privacy threat.
assumptions: The backend process is modeled as a Process element, and the secondary guardian is an ExternalEntity.

title: Data-Centric Threat
description: The data flow (DF11) transmits live location data from the backend (P1) to the secondary guardian (EE3). This data-centric threat arises because the data is being shared with an external entity without a valid modeled flow. The act of sharing data with an external entity without a valid modeled flow creates a privacy threat.
assumptions: The data flow (DF11) is modeled, and the data being transmitted is live location data.

title: Unauthorized Access
description: The secondary guardian (EE3) receives the live location data from the backend (P1). This external entity receives data and processes or stores it in a way that causes a privacy threat, as it is an external entity without a valid modeled flow to the backend.
assumptions: The secondary guardian (EE3) is modeled as an ExternalEntity element.

title: Unauthorized Access to Aggregated Data
description: The process P1 shares aggregated usage and engagement analytics with an external entity (EE4). If the partner lacks appropriate access controls or if the data is not encrypted in transit, an unauthorized party could access this sensitive information.
assumptions: The partner is not configured with the necessary permissions to view the data.

title: Data in Transit
description: The data flow DF12 carries aggregated usage and engagement analytics between the backend and the advertising partner. If the data is not encrypted in transit, it could be intercepted or modified by third parties.
assumptions: The data is not encrypted in transit.

title: Unauthorized Use of Data
description: The external entity EE4 receives the analytics data and may use it for purposes other than the intended advertising/analytics partnership, such as selling user data to third parties or using it for their own marketing campaigns.
assumptions: The partner has not agreed to the specific use of the data.

title: Attributable Data Evidence
description: The Child (ExternalEntity EE2) sends a manual check-in/SOS message with their current location to the parent (Process P1). This action attributes the data (the message and its associated location data) to the user, creating a non-repudiation risk where the parent cannot deny the message's existence or the user's intent.
assumptions: The message is successfully transmitted and the parent receives it.

title: Data Processing and Storage
description: The parent (Process P1) receives the SOS message and processes it. This action may involve storing the message or location data, creating a potential privacy risk where the parent could misuse, retain, or disclose the data in ways not intended by the Child.
assumptions: The parent processes the message as intended.
